description: Hi, I’m Brit, an AI Software Engineering student and human-centered builder working with Google Cloud, Gemini, ADK, React, and Web Audio. I love turning dense technical data into intuitive, accessible experiences that spark curiosity. For "Abandoned but not Forgotten," I’m building an interactive, story-driven experience that gives NASA’s Moon and Mars hardware a voice, blending real mission science with creative design so anyone can explore the stories left behind in space.
summary: Voices of the Silent Fleet is an interactive, story-driven web application built for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge that transforms NASA's historic lunar, Martian, and deep-space hardware into first-person storytellers. Rather than viewing deactivated or distant spacecraft as forgotten debris, learners explore a logarithmic Celestial Scale Explorer spanning the Moon (Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector), Mars (Opportunity Rover "Oppy," InSight Lander, and Ingenuity Helicopter "Ginny"), and Interstellar Space (Voyager 1), alongside our 2026 Earth Mission Control relay ("Devcraftsman"). Each spacecraft profile pairs verified NASA Science Mission Directorate, NSSDC, PDS, and JPL telemetry with a three-chapter narrative timeline and an interactive AI storyteller powered by Google Gemini. Students and curious explorers can ask questions in plain language and receive scientifically grounded, in-character answers, bridging real orbital data and human engineering to inspire the next generation of space builders.
details:
### Inspiration & Challenge Alignment

Historic NASA spacecraft continue teaching humanity long after their primary missions end—from Apollo 11's passive retroreflector still returning laser pulses after 57+ years, to Opportunity's 45.16 km Martian marathon, InSight's 1,319 recorded marsquakes, Ingenuity's 72 aerial flights, and Voyager 1's ongoing journey past 24.9 billion km. Voices of the Silent Fleet makes these milestones tangible and memorable for school-age learners and the public through interactive storytelling.

### How It Works

1. Logarithmic Celestial Scale Explorer: Compares each spacecraft's real distance from Earth and one-way light travel time (1.28 light-seconds to 22+ light-hours).

2. 3-Chapter Mission Dossiers & Science Field Notes: Breaks down each mission's deployment, breakthrough discoveries, and lasting scientific legacy using official COSPAR/NSSDC identifiers and landing coordinates.

3. First-Person Gemini Storyteller: Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Node.js/Express, using Google Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash) with mission-grounded system prompts so every conversation stays faithful to verified NASA archives.
